planting.note: Pot up divisions or rooted cuttings in spring once nighttime temperatures stay above 60°F; grows year-round indoors.

directions: Grow in a loose, peaty mix that stays evenly moist, since the thin leaves wilt dramatically within hours of drying out. Give bright, indirect light only; the deep green blades and their contrasting purple-red veining scorch quickly under direct sun. Pot in shallow, wide containers that suit the shallow root system, and raise humidity with a pebble tray or terrarium setting to prevent crisped leaf margins. Pinch growing tips regularly to keep the naturally sprawling stems compact and full rather than leggy.
sources: North Carolina State University Extension — Plant Toolbox: Fittonia albivenis

planting.note: Divide and repot rhizome clumps in spring as new growth resumes; otherwise keep as a year-round indoor plant.

directions: Native to Central American rainforest understories, this smaller peace lily species carries glossy elliptic-oblong leaves on long thin petioles below a pale green, narrow-hooded spathe and cream spadix. Keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged, since drooping leaves are its clearest signal that a drink is overdue. Provide warm temperatures and bright, filtered light well away from direct sun, which bleaches the foliage. Wipe leaves occasionally to remove dust and support the plant's natural air-purifying habit indoors.
sources: Kew Royal Botanic Gardens — Plants of the World Online: Spathiphyllum blandum

planting.note: Divide crowded clumps or pot up rooted offsets in spring; grown as a year-round houseplant.

directions: 'Black Lance' is a freely branching, upright Aglaonema selection carrying long, narrow leaves dominated by a broad silver-green center flanked by darker green chevron edging. Its tall habit and rapid growth make it a good floor or desk accent in low-to-moderate interior light, though it colors up more richly with bright indirect exposure. Let the top inch of potting mix dry between waterings, since this cultivar resents soggy soil and is noted for strong resistance to the leaf diseases that trouble other Aglaonema. Wear gloves when dividing or pruning, as the sap contains irritating calcium oxalate crystals.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Aglaonema

planting.note: Divide offsets or pot rooted stem cuttings in spring; grown as a year-round houseplant.

directions: Bred from Southeast Asian and New Guinea lines, 'Maria Christina' resembles the familiar 'Silver Queen' but stays denser and more compact, with slender light-green leaves edged in silvery white. It tolerates lower light and cooler room temperatures than many Aglaonema selections, making it forgiving in offices or shaded interiors. Water only once the surface soil dries slightly, and avoid cold drafts below roughly 55°F, which can blacken the foliage. Repot every couple of years as clumping stems fill the container, refreshing the potting mix to maintain vigor.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Aglaonema

planting.note: Divide rhizome clumps in spring as new growth begins; otherwise grown year-round indoors.

directions: Native to Peruvian rainforest understory, this prayer-plant relative opens dark green young leaves pin-striped in pale pink and white, fading toward solid green as each leaf ages while the underside stays purple throughout its life. Keep it out of direct sun, which scorches the thin foliage, and favor bright filtered light instead. Water with room-temperature or filtered water to keep soil evenly moist, and run a humidifier or pebble tray nearby since dry indoor air causes crisp brown leaf edges. This species is frequently mislabeled and sold under the 'Calathea ornata' trade name, so confirm the striping pattern described here before assuming the two are identical.
sources: Kew Royal Botanic Gardens — Plants of the World Online: Goeppertia sanderiana
